High-pressure CsCl-type B2 RbCl. The phase is not quenchable to zero pressure. The lattice is therefore the hypothetical zero-pressure reference implied by Campbell and Heinz's rho02=3.3068(10) Mg/m^3, not a directly observed ambient cell.

## Campbell and Heinz (1994), RbCl-B2 BM3

Identifier: `rbcl_b2_campbell_1994_bm3_1`.

Availability: **Executable**.

Automatic selection for equilibrium calculations.


- **Origin of the parameterization:** experimental
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Campbell; Heinz
    - **Year:** 1994
    - **Title:** High-pressure acoustic wave velocities and equations of state of the alkali chlorides
    - **Source:** J. Geophys. Res.
    - **Volume:** 99
    - **Locator:** 11765-11774
    - **DOI:** 10.1029/94JB00127
- **Reference temperature (K):** 298.0
- **Reported pressure coverage (GPa):** \[1.11, 32.3\]
- **Coverage provenance:** reported\_exactly

| Component | Parameter | Value | Reported error | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary | V0 | 60.7214565241 | 0.0183626033 | Yes |
| Primary | K0 | 17.9 | 1.0 | Not listed |
| Primary | K0\_prime | 5.23 | 0.29 | Not listed |

Values use the source model's parameter units. Primary `V0` uses
the conventional-cell volume declared above. Errors retain their reported
meaning; an absent error is unknown, and absence of covariance does not
establish statistical independence.

Room-temperature third-order Birch-Murnaghan fit to all 24 RbCl-B2 compression observations in Table 1. Campbell and Heinz fixed the non-quenchable phase's hypothetical zero-pressure density at rho02=3.3068(10) Mg/m^3 and report K0=17.9(10) GPa and K0'=5.23(29). Peritheos converts that density to the one-formula-unit reference volume using M(RbCl)=120.9208 g/mol; its uncertainty is propagated from the reported density error.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

Published preferred case 1; no coefficients are replaced by an independent fit. Parameter errors retain printed estimated standard deviations; covariance and confidence level are unavailable. Source molar and cell V0 uncertainties disagree after unit conversion (especially RbCl); canonical values/errors are converted from the molar row actually used by EoSFit7; both printed forms are retained. Rounded coefficients do not reproduce every benchmark at the last printed ratio digit. Full covariance, original EoSFit7 inputs, and raw GSAS projects were not exposed by the retrieved public deposit. Supplement footnotes cite Decker 1973 and Matsui 2007 whereas main references cite Decker 1971 and Matsui 2009. Historical CsCl Vinet-MGD coefficients and GUI defaults are recovered; the saved runtime settings and five pressure discrepancies remain unresolved.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Hybrid: experimentally fitted DAC/LVP parameters with fixed Debye temperatures derived from DFT elastic constants of Haddadi et al. (2009), as explicitly described in the official supplement. Main-text reference 41 instead lists Kumara Swamy et al. (1996); the supplement resolves the actual calculation source.
- **Equation:** Main Eqs. (1), (6)-(9): 300 K BM3 plus gamma(V)\[ED(V,T)-ED(V,300)\]/V; theta=theta0 exp\[(gamma0-gamma)/q\], gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q. Integrated law, not theta0(V/V0)^\[-gamma(V)\].
- **V0:** Table I, case 1: fixed DAC-derived 36.25 +/- 0.03 cm^3/mol; convert by 1e24/NA to the Z=1 conventional cell. Printed cell alternative 60.2 +/- 0.02 A^3 retained without replacing the molar value.
- **K0:** Table I, case 1: freely fitted with weighted P,V,T errors using EoSFit7.
- **K0 prime:** Table I, case 1: freely fitted with weighted P,V,T errors using EoSFit7.
- **Gamma0:** Table I, case 1: fitted jointly with K0, K0\_prime, q; V0 and theta0 fixed.
- **Q:** Table I, case 1; Eq. (9), logarithmic volume dependence of gamma.
- **Theta0:** Table I and supplement section 1: 177 K fixed; DFT elastic constants via Haddadi et al. (2009), not a free fit parameter.
- **N:** Eq. (7): two atoms per formula unit. Z=1, so two atoms per conventional Pm-3m cell.
- **Tr:** Main text section 3 and Eqs. (2),(6): 300 K.

</details>
